title: GATE – High-Intensity Group Therapy EMDR for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: A Randomized Feasibility Trial of a Two-Week Outpatient G-TEP–Based Intensive Treatment Compared With a Three-Month Waitlist
summary:
Background: People who have experienced very distressing or traumatic events may continue to experience psychological difficulties long afterwards. The GATE study investigates a shortened, high-intensity outpatient EMDR-group treatment in which distressing memories are specifically addressed.

Research question: The study investigates whether the intensive treatment can be provided effectively in outpatient care within two weeks and whether it is well accepted by participants. It will also examine how safe and helpful the treatment is and whether trauma-related symptoms and psychological difficulties can be meaningfully reduced and sleep, well-being, and quality of life improved.

Methods: After a detailed assessment, adult participants will be randomly assigned to a group receiving treatment immediately or to a group receiving treatment at a later time. The treatment consists of eight group sessions within two weeks and an additional session after three months. At several time points, participants will complete questionnaires on psychological difficulties, trauma-related symptoms, sleep, well-being, and quality of life. The results will be scientifically evaluated to provide information for future treatment services and research studies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Fulfilment of the diagnostic criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder, complex post-traumatic stress disorder, or F43.8, confirmed by a structured clinical interview (DIPS).
2. Minimum symptom severity, defined as an IES-R score of ≥24.
3. Written informed consent or electronic informed consent (e-consent) to participate in the study.
4. Ability to provide informed consent.
5. Age ≥18 years.
6. Sufficient German language skills to participate in the group therapy sessions.
7. Access to internal resources, e.g. memories of safe or strengthening experiences.
8. Willingness and ability to participate in resource-oriented exercises and imagery techniques (e.g. visualization of a safe place), which are essential therapeutic components of the program.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute suicidality or acute risk of self-harm or harm to others.
2. Severe comorbid psychiatric disorders (e.g. psychotic disorders, dissociative identity disorder, acute substance dependence).
3. Cognitive impairment (e.g. dementia, organic brain syndrome, severe cognitive impairment).
4. Current use of benzodiazepines.
5. Ongoing changes in medication.
6. Prescription of medical cannabis containing THC.
7. Severe unstable medical conditions or neurological disorders (e.g. active cancer requiring treatment).
8. Concurrent psychotherapy.
9. Known pregnancy.
10. Insufficient German language skills to participate in group sessions.
11. Severe dissociative symptoms (SDQ-20 >35 or DES-B >2).
